svg.font-family: Segoe UI, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: XPU2: an asynchronous CPU + GPU path tracer for MoonRay previews
Private test build, as of session 99 (25 October 2026). One work grid; each device takes its own work; what the GPU cannot render goes to the CPU sample by sample.
Modo + private MoonRay kit
Preferences > XPU2 picks the GPU renderer
preview session, persistent protocol v1
Denoiser, Smart Render, Safe Denoising
outlines: CPU workers blue, GPU workers violet
final renders, LS, MoonLightIPR: MoonRay as before
moonray_xpu2.exe (preview session)
RDL scene and deltas (RDLB mesh arrays)
frames, drain, hold, cancel; pictures via shared memory
checkpoints: .safe.exr saves, "Wrote:" lines
a frame's timeline; GPU profile by stage
tile and worker outlines (@@MODO_GPU_WORKERS)
MoonRay XPU (fallback)
a scene with an entity XPU2 does not render
(deep output, a camera medium, ...)
@@MODO_XPU2 FALLBACK <reason>
the Render Log says why
XPU2 takes the scene back once it can
Scene indexer
canonical session: every RDL object and attribute, kept incrementally
classifier (entity_classes.h): each object is Both, CPU only or Fallback,
with the GPU feature families it needs (DwaBase, layers, hair, glitter,
toon, subsurface, maps, curves, points, motion, volumes, VDB ...)
router: a decision per entity, redone only for what an edit touched
→ the scene's mode: fallback · CPU only (light filters, shadow links,
emissive volumes) · both devices
Plan builder (cpu::prepare)
meshes reused by signature; each carries the indexer's families
xpu2_geom.dll: MoonRay's PolyMesh / OpenSubdiv tessellation, displacement
materials → records and map programs (DwaBase trees, 70 map types)
lights, light tree, light filters · volumes, NanoVDB grids
textures: host mip pyramids · AOV plan: LPEs, material and state
AOVs, Cryptomatte, checkpoint and resume names
bounce-ray reuse: which ray types meet the shadow rays' occluders
refused: mode fallback
Renderer (async_render.h)
Cells by suitability (device_suit.h)
a first-hit probe, four camera rays a tile
each cell: the GPU's probability of being its
efficient owner (families, deferrals, lane rates)
owners by comparative advantage
Important parts first
the pictures score each cell (MoonRay's tile score)
above the mean: kept by its owner, a range ahead
the rest: open to either device, most important first
Work grid (async_grid.h)
8 px tiles in 64 px cells, chunks of samples
progressive ranges 1, 1, 2, then 4 samples
a frontier per device: nothing past its least-
sampled range (the whole picture first)
Cellular workers on both devices
CPU threads and 32 GPU workers (a launch's shares)
finish the cell · own reserved · open · by passage
ownership flips follow the measured shares
Rights of passage
CPU into GPU cells: its chunk ends before the GPU
would get there, or the GPU has not claimed lately
GPU into CPU cells: the CPU's backlog outlasts four
launches, where it would not mostly defer
Launches and adaptive sampling
launches of at least 2 samples a thread
cellular generations (default) or MoonRay's trees
checkpoints: the frame so far, every interval
the plan
CPU lane (async_cpu.h)
persistent workers move by the cellular rules
Embree: surfaces, and volume bounds (VDB leaf cells
gated by the active-voxel box)
renders every feature XPU2 has, including what the GPU
defers: points, geometry in motion, VDB, heterogeneous
and emissive volumes
retry queue: samples the GPU deferred, each rendered
whole from its identity (no path state crosses devices)
provisional samples rendered again in full (every texture
level is in RAM), their values settled out of the GPU's
provisional film
textures read from host RAM
light filters, shadow linking, lobe light sets, lights in
motion and emissive volumes keep a whole scene on the CPU
(Embree's occlusion and intersection agree, as on the GPU)
GPU lane (async_gpu.h, OptiX 7.6)
a mailbox ring of chunks, two launches in flight
surfaces IAS, a GAS per mesh (kept while unchanged)
stand-ins and VDB / emissive volumes defer samples
to the CPU lane through the deferred ring
textures: VRAM holds mip levels 1+ and a 512 MB LRU
cache of level-0 tiles from RAM
partial shading: a missing tile's texel read from its
parent a level up; the sample is provisional (its own
film, a record to the host), rendered again in full
Cryptomatte and the closest filter merged without locks
the program in 9 modules, compiled by OptiX in parallel:
path tracer · material · maps · lights · lobes · volumes
(continuation callables) · DwaBase resolve · DwaBase
lobes · extras (camera, AOVs) · 3.5 minutes cold
no OptiX call inside the map callable (compile time)
chunks its workers claim
chunks its cellular workers claim
deferred samples
(pixel, index, pass)
provisional samples
(pixel, index, tile, value)
back to the GPU once
their tile has landed
Shared integrator (async_integrator.h)
MoonRay's path tracer and shader library, ported: one source compiled for both devices (X2_HD), with MoonRay's vector-mode quirks reproduced where they show
every sample's random numbers come from its identity (pixel, sample index, seed), so either device makes the same sample
bounce-ray reuse: a BSDF sample that reaches a light and goes on needs no shadow ray: its bounce's nearest hit decides
Film
both lanes' samples merged: beauty, alpha, AOVs, light path expressions, Cryptomatte, display filters (MoonRay's own DSOs)
provisional samples shown in the pictures, kept out of the film, none left at the frame's end (audited)
pictures: pixels no sample has reached filled from their neighbours (display only)
Outputs to the kit
beauty and the denoiser's guides (albedo, normal) → the kit's denoiser (OptiX or Open Image Denoise)
Smart Render stops by a drain · Safe Denoising keeps the last save · Continue starts XPU2 again (no resume yet)
